chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the earth cannot be empty of a Divine Authority (Hujja), and I, by God, am that Divine Authority.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan — Title of Imam Ali al-Hadi (AS), the 10th Imam
key_terms.الْأَرْض: al-ard — The earth; the inhabited world that must always have a Hujja
key_terms.حُجَّة: Hujja — Divine Authority, Proof; the Imam as God's proof on earth

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali al-Hadi say about the earth never being empty of a Divine Authority?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Hadi (AS), the 10th Imam, declares to his companion Abu Ali ibn Rashid that the earth is never without a Hujja (Divine Authority, Proof of God), and he personally affirms — with an oath by God — that he himself is that Hujja. This is a foundational Shia creedal statement asserting the perpetual necessity of an Imam on earth at all times, and the Imam's self-identification as the living proof of God in his era. For the Shia faithful, this statement would have been received as the Imam's authoritative declaration of his own divine mandate.
